title: Implement typed mutation, audit, and claim synchronization
description:
Make `repository_state` the sole typed-to-byte finalizer for every repository-owned record — issues, index membership, neutral registry declarations, profile provenance, gate-run/audit artifacts, and events — with deterministic identifiers and exact lifecycle timestamps, and route claim acquire's repository-side issue/event synchronization through the same recovered session. This builds on the layout-aware store, kernel, and recovery already on the integration branch.

## Background

Commands currently stamp identifiers and timestamps and publish issue, event, and gate-run bytes through independent storage calls, so a rebuild can change IDs, a lifecycle migration can overwrite historical time, and claim acquire can leave an issue assigned while its claim event is absent. This package concentrates all typed serialization, time/ID authority, and audit append into `repository_state`, published through one delta.

## What to build

- Typed mutation identity and time authority: `repository_state` is the sole finalizer for issue upserts/deletes, deterministic `index.json` membership (issue creation, deletion, and restore derive exact `all_ids`/`deleted_ids` from the captured index preimage in the same delta), neutral registry declarations, profile provenance, gate-run/audit artifacts, and events. Commands submit timestamp-free, identifier-free semantic intents. A `MutationContext` holding an injected `IdAuthority` and `MutationClock` is created exactly once after canonical session acquisition and reused unchanged when closure expansion or conflict recovery rebuilds the operation. Production samples its UUID/random source once; memory and tests inject a deterministic seed. Allocation order is frozen: new issue identifiers first in canonical request order (so expected-absent `Data(Descendant("issues/<id>.json"))` paths enter `CaptureSpec` before capture), transaction-visible gate-run/profile/other record identifiers next in `(target, key)` order, event identifiers last after canonical event ordering. Every allocated identity and the context seed enter the semantic plan hash; no retry or backend resamples them.
- Exact lifecycle timestamp semantics: for a non-noop mutation the context samples one `MutationTimestamp` once; the finalizer applies it only to transitions that occur — creation sets `created_at`/`updated_at` (and `first_ready_at` when initially Ready), later semantic changes set `updated_at`, the first Ready transition sets `first_ready_at`, claim/completion set `claimed_at`/`done_at`, and a created/changed `GateState` sets its `updated_at`. Existing lifecycle values are preserved when their transition does not occur. External checker `started_at`/`completed_at` remain captured evidence; lifecycle migration reconstructs historical fields only from captured history, never the current clock. No-op operations sample neither IDs nor time and emit no bytes. Delete the ID/time-generating `Issue::new`, `Issue::new_with_labels`, and production `Event::new_*` seed use; tests use explicit deterministic fixture builders with no compatibility constructors.
- Canonical audit append: the finalizer takes the exact captured `Data(Descendant("events.jsonl"))` prefix, owns malformed/torn-tail detection, preserves every prefix byte, adds exactly one newline separator only when a non-empty prefix lacks one, orders semantic event intents by `(mutation phase, event tag, primary identity, secondary identity, command-local ordinal)`, assigns their IDs last through `IdAuthority`, and appends each with one trailing newline. The finalizer — not command code — sets `ProfileApplied.isolated_torn_tail` from its inspection of that prefix. The exact preimage/final bytes, listing identity, event identities, and torn-tail evidence enter the same plan hash, delta, and transaction, preserving `@/inv/event-log`. Delete init's torn-tail/event-construction helper, `append_profile_event_image`, and every command-local event JSON/image helper; there is no alternate append path for repository-owned events.
- Git-required claim synchronization: claim acquire holds coordinator while opening the recovered session and applying the idempotent repository-side issue/event transition (yielding coordinator → bootstrap → repository → events); reverse acquisition is rejected. Lease operations without repository-side effects (release, renew, heartbeat, force-evict) remain coordinator-only. The repository transition is derived from the captured image and convergent over both the captured issue state and event-log tail: when both already reflect the claim, acquire is a complete no-op; when a prior split path left the issue assigned but the claim event absent, the retry emits exactly the missing event; a duplicate event is never emitted (preserving `@/inv/event-log`). Acquire resolves the issue id to its canonical full id and passes that canonical id to the coordinator; lease matching canonicalizes the issue identity of persisted lease records during comparison, so an active lease recorded under a short-ID spelling is recognized and never duplicated by a full-ID acquire. Under the coordinator lock, acquire reconciles the derived `claims.index.json` against the append-only claims log before lease creation, so a lease durably appended by a crash-interrupted attempt is recognized even when the derived index was never published.

Distilled §2 contracts: typed mutation identity and time authority, exact lifecycle timestamp semantics, canonical audit append, and Git-required claim synchronization. See `dev/active/cdc840ad-plan.md` §2 and plan decisions D5, D15, D19 for full detail. Git remains optional for core commands but required for claims (`@/charter/D-4`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Typed issue/gate/provenance/event bytes and exact timestamps/IDs are deterministic across both backends; no-op operations sample neither IDs nor time.
- [hard] REQ-02: Claim and crash tests prove coordinator-held acquire synchronization, idempotent retry, reverse-order rejection, coordinator-only release/renew/heartbeat, and an unchanged lease format and command surface.

## Constraints

- Invoker-approved delivery model (2026-07-19): cumulative final-form wave commits land directly on `main`. The retired `integration/cdc840ad` branch is not authoritative and no integration-only final transition is required. Each commit runs targeted tests plus all prior cumulative package tests on both backends.
- No adapter, feature flag, compatibility re-export, dual path, temporary API, or independent `append_event`/`save_issue`/`save_gate_run` publisher survives.
- Out of scope (plan D19/D20): lease credential surface, claim-log format, and claim-command set are unchanged — this package synchronizes only the repository-side issue/event state through the shared transaction; leases stay in `.git/jit` outside the repository transaction. No worktree/data-root binding redesign.

Blast radius: domain events/queries, the claim coordinator repository-sync path, mutation producers, and conformance tests.

## Scope amendment (invoker-approved, 2026-07-19)

Boundary per the approved breakdown: this package builds the typed mutation, identity/time authority, canonical audit append, and finalizer machinery, and migrates exactly one producer — claim acquire's repository-side issue/event synchronization. Migration of the remaining command producers and the deletion of `Issue::new`, `Issue::new_with_labels`, production `Event::new_*` use, and the independent `append_event`/`save_issue`/`save_gate_run` publishers belong to "Migrate all consumers and delete predecessors" (49adf23b), whose text states "Deletion happens here — not deferred." Until then those constructors and publishers are frozen deletion debt: this package's new paths must not use them and must add no new callers, so the wave-5 deletion is a pure caller-swap. The deletion sentences in "What to build" state the end state wave 5 completes.
